dialogue.realtalk: You want to talk? Alright. What's on your mind?
dialogue.realtalk/1: Sure, we can talk. What about?
dialogue.realtalk/2: I'm listening. What do you want to know?
dialogue.realtalk.work: Do you actually like your work?
dialogue.realtalk.feelings: How do you really feel about me?
dialogue.realtalk.checkin.good: Honestly? Pretty good. The bread turned out right and nobody's yelled at me yet.
dialogue.realtalk.checkin.good/1: Better now that someone actually asked. Most folks just want directions.
dialogue.realtalk.checkin.good/2: Can't complain. Slept through the night, and the roof only leaks in one spot now.
dialogue.realtalk.checkin.rough: You want the honest answer? It's been a heavy few days. Thanks for asking, %1$s.
dialogue.realtalk.checkin.rough/1: Not my best morning. But you asking helps more than you'd think.
dialogue.realtalk.checkin.again: You asked me that this morning, %1$s. Still the same answer.
dialogue.realtalk.checkin.again/1: Twice in one day? Either you care a lot or you forgot you asked.
dialogue.realtalk.day.good: Good one, actually. The well water was cold and the queue at the smith was short.
dialogue.realtalk.day.good/1: It's the kind of day where the chickens behave. I'll take it.
dialogue.realtalk.day.good/2: Sun's out, boots are dry. That's a win around here.
dialogue.realtalk.day.rough: Long. My back aches and the cat knocked the stew off the table.
dialogue.realtalk.day.rough/1: One of those days where the door sticks and everything else follows its lead.
dialogue.realtalk.day.working: Busy hands today. Ask me again when I've put this down.
dialogue.realtalk.day.working/1: In the middle of it, as you can see. But it's honest work.
dialogue.realtalk.day.again: Same day it was an hour ago, %1$s.
dialogue.realtalk.day.again/1: Still going. Days don't change that fast around here.
dialogue.realtalk.work.like: I do, most days. There's a rhythm to it. You stop noticing the blisters.
dialogue.realtalk.work.like/1: It's mine, you know? Nobody tells me how to run my own bench.
dialogue.realtalk.work.like/2: Ask me at dawn and I'll grumble. Ask me when it's done and I'm proud of it.
dialogue.realtalk.work.hate: Between us? Some mornings I stare at the ceiling and think about just... walking.
dialogue.realtalk.work.hate/1: It pays for bread. That's the nicest thing I can say about it.
dialogue.realtalk.work.again: We covered my work already. It hasn't gotten more interesting since.
dialogue.realtalk.village.home: %2$s? It's home. The bell's cracked and the gossip's fast, but it's home.
dialogue.realtalk.village.home/1: I know every fence post in %2$s. Some days that's comfort, some days it's a cage.
dialogue.realtalk.village.none: I don't really have a place. I go where the road goes.
dialogue.realtalk.village.none/1: No village claims me right now. It's quieter that way, mostly lonelier.
dialogue.realtalk.village.again: Still the same village, %1$s. The fences haven't moved.
dialogue.realtalk.life.first: My life? Nobody's asked me that before. Give me a second... it's a long story with a lot of turnips in it.
dialogue.realtalk.life.first/1: Where do I even start? Born here, scraped knees here, buried my father behind the chapel. Still here.
dialogue.realtalk.life.first/2: It's been quiet mostly. One flood, one bad winter, one summer I still think about.
dialogue.realtalk.life.revisit: You asked me about my life once. I've been thinking about what I left out.
dialogue.realtalk.life.revisit/1: Remember when you asked about my life? I remembered the good parts after you left.
dialogue.realtalk.life.again: I just told you my whole story. Let it breathe a little.
dialogue.realtalk.dreams.first: Don't laugh. I want to see the ocean once. Just once. Smell the salt.
dialogue.realtalk.dreams.first/1: I dream about a bigger garden. And once, flying. The garden feels more likely.
dialogue.realtalk.dreams.first/2: Someday I want to build something that outlasts me. A bridge, maybe. Or a family.
dialogue.realtalk.dreams.revisit: Still dreaming about what I told you. It hasn't gotten smaller.
dialogue.realtalk.dreams.again: You know my dream already. Saying it twice won't make it come faster.
dialogue.realtalk.dreams.encourage.glad: You think so? Then maybe I'll actually do it. Watch me, %1$s.
dialogue.realtalk.dreams.encourage.glad/: Careful — encourage me and I might drag you along.
dialogue.realtalk.dreams.encourage.doubt: That's kind. But dreams cost coin, and mine's mostly spoken for.
dialogue.realtalk.dreams.more: More? Alright. In the dream there's a porch, and nobody needs anything from me until noon.
dialogue.realtalk.fears.first: Honestly? Thunder. And the thing that scratched at my door two winters back. Mostly the thunder.
dialogue.realtalk.fears.first/1: Being forgotten. Everyone remembers the mayor. Nobody remembers who fixed the well.
dialogue.realtalk.fears.first/2: The dark past the last lantern. Everyone pretends they're not afraid of it. They're lying.
dialogue.realtalk.fears.revisit: I've been chewing on what you asked me — about being afraid. It's lighter now that it's said.
dialogue.realtalk.fears.again: I already showed you that scar, %1$s. Don't poke it twice in one week.
dialogue.realtalk.fears.comfort.thanks: ...Thank you. Most people change the subject.
dialogue.realtalk.fears.comfort.brushoff: I'm fine. Forget I said anything. The thunder and I have an understanding.
dialogue.realtalk.fears.share.grateful: You too? Huh. It's less heavy when two people carry it.
dialogue.realtalk.fears.share.grateful/1: Strange comfort, that. Two cowards make one brave pair.
dialogue.realtalk.fears.share.joke: Then we'll hide under the same table when it storms. Bring bread.
dialogue.realtalk.feelings.first: You're really asking? Fine. You're the part of my day I don't complain about.
dialogue.realtalk.feelings.first/1: I notice when you don't come around. That's my answer.
dialogue.realtalk.feelings.spouse: You're my whole ledger, %1$s. Every column. Even the messy ones.
dialogue.realtalk.feelings.spouse/1: Married you, didn't I? But since you're asking — I'd do it again tomorrow.
dialogue.realtalk.feelings.again: I laid my heart on the table already. Give it a day to recover.
dialogue.realtalk.feelings.unsure: I'm not sure how I feel yet.
dialogue.realtalk.feelings.same.happy: Then say it more often, %1$s. Words like that keep better than bread.
dialogue.realtalk.feelings.same.shy: Oh. I... need to go stand somewhere else and smile for a bit.
dialogue.realtalk.feelings.unsure.hurt: Right. Well. Thank you for the honesty, I suppose.
dialogue.realtalk.feelings.unsure.patien: That's fair. I'm not going anywhere. Take your time.
dialogue.realtalk.regrets.first: One or two. There was a door I didn't knock on, years ago. I still walk past it.
dialogue.realtalk.regrets.first/1: I regret the things I didn't say at a funeral once. Say your things, %1$s.
dialogue.realtalk.regrets.first/2: I traded a friendship for pride once. Worst deal I ever made.
dialogue.realtalk.regrets.again: We turned those stones over already. Let them lie a while.
dialogue.realtalk.deflect.personal: That's... a bit close to the bone for someone I barely know.
dialogue.realtalk.deflect.personal/1: Maybe when I know you better, %1$s. Words like that need trust first.
dialogue.realtalk.deflect.personal/2: Buy me a sweetroll first. Then we'll see about the deep questions.
dialogue.realtalk.deflect.personal/3: I keep that shelf locked. Come back when we're friends, not acquaintances.
dialogue.realtalk.deflect.intimate: That question belongs to someone I trust with everything. We're not there.
dialogue.realtalk.deflect.intimate/1: Ask me again when you've earned it, %1$s. That one costs more than hearts on a sleeve.
dialogue.realtalk.deflect.intimate/2: Some doors open slowly. Keep showing up and maybe.
dialogue.realtalk.gossip.marriage: You didn't hear it from me, but %2$s and %3$s got married! The whole square's been buzzing.
dialogue.realtalk.gossip.marriage/1: Big news — %2$s finally married %3$s. About time, if you ask anyone with eyes.
dialogue.realtalk.gossip.divorce: Keep it quiet, but %2$s and %3$s split up. Nobody's saying why and everybody's guessing.
dialogue.realtalk.gossip.divorce/1: %2$s and %3$s aren't together anymore. The baker knew before either of them did, I swear.
dialogue.realtalk.gossip.death: Sad news, I'm afraid. We lost %2$s. The village feels smaller without them.
dialogue.realtalk.gossip.death/1: You heard about %2$s? Gone. Folks left flowers by the well.
dialogue.realtalk.gossip.birth: Happy news for once — there's a new baby! Little %2$s. Loudest lungs in the village.
dialogue.realtalk.gossip.birth/1: Have you seen the baby yet? %2$s. Even the grumpy ones stopped to smile.
dialogue.realtalk.gossip.none: Quiet week, honestly. The most exciting thing was a chicken on the chapel roof.
dialogue.realtalk.gossip.none/1: Nothing new. Same faces, same fences. I'd trade an ear for some real news.
dialogue.realtalk.us.future: What do you want for our future?
dialogue.realtalk.us.happy.yes: With you? Yes. Even when you track mud in. Especially then, somehow.
dialogue.realtalk.us.happy.yes/1: I catch myself humming while I work. That's your fault, %1$s.
dialogue.realtalk.us.happy.low: I'm happy with you. It's everything else that's been heavy lately.
dialogue.realtalk.us.happy.grateful: Happy? You brought me %2$s and asked me that with a straight face. Yes, love. Yes.
dialogue.realtalk.us.happy.grateful/1: Still smiling about that %2$s, if I'm honest. You know me too well.
dialogue.realtalk.us.firstmet.memory: Of course. You looked completely lost, and I pretended I wasn't staring. Best day %2$s ever had.
dialogue.realtalk.us.firstmet.memory/1: You had the wrong boots for the weather and the right smile for me. I remember all of it.
dialogue.realtalk.us.firstmet.again: We just walked down that road, love. But I never mind the view.
dialogue.realtalk.us.future.together: More mornings like this one. Maybe a bigger table. People to sit at it.
dialogue.realtalk.us.future.together/1: I want us old and insufferable on a porch somewhere, judging everyone's fences.
dialogue.realtalk.us.future.baby: Right now? I mostly think about the little one coming. Terrified. Thrilled. Both.
dialogue.realtalk.us.future.kids: I want the kids to have it easier than we did. That's the whole plan, really.
dialogue.realtalk.us.worries.open: Since you ask... yes. I didn't want to burden you, but yes. Sit with me a moment.
dialogue.realtalk.us.worries.open/1: There's a weight I've been carrying quietly. I should have told you sooner.
dialogue.realtalk.us.worries.fine: Nothing worth your frown. The usual aches. Having you ask is half the cure.
dialogue.realtalk.us.worries.again: You checked on me already, love. I promise I'd tell you.
dialogue.realtalk.family.checkin_child: How are you holding up, little one?
dialogue.realtalk.family.ask_parent: Can I ask you something? Parent to child?
dialogue.realtalk.family.child.little: Up! Up! I found a bug and it's my friend now!
dialogue.realtalk.family.child.little/1: I'm gonna be tall tomorrow. I decided.
dialogue.realtalk.family.child.teen: I'm fine. Everyone keeps asking. I'm FINE. ...Thanks for asking, though.
dialogue.realtalk.family.child.teen/1: Can I have more responsibility and also no responsibility? Is that a thing?
dialogue.realtalk.family.child.doing: Pretty good! I beat the miller's kid at races twice. TWICE.
dialogue.realtalk.family.parent.proud: You turned out well, you know. I don't say it enough. I'm saying it now.
dialogue.realtalk.family.parent.proud/1: Ask away. Though watching you lately, you need less advice than you think.
dialogue.realtalk.family.parent.worried: I worry, that's all. It's the job. You never stop being someone's parent.
dialogue.realtalk.family.memories.share: Did I ever tell you about the winter %2$s got snowed into the outhouse? No? Sit down.
dialogue.realtalk.family.memories.share/: There's a story about %2$s and a runaway pig that this family swore to keep secret. Anyway—
dialogue.realtalk.family.memories.again: I told you the good one already. The rest need supper and a fire to come out right.
dialogue.main/9: I've got a few minutes before someone needs something.
dialogue.main/11: You've got that look. What is it this time?
dialogue.main/12: Talk to me. The turnips can wait.
dialogue.greet.success/6: There's a face I don't mind seeing.
dialogue.greet.success/7: Morning, noon, whatever it is — good to see you, %1$s.
dialogue.greet.success/8: Well met. You picked a fine day to exist.
dialogue.greet.success/9: Ah, %1$s! I was just thinking the day needed improving.
dialogue.greet.fail/6: Oh. It's you. I was hoping for the bread cart.
dialogue.greet.fail/8: If this is about the fence, I already know.
dialogue.chat.success/20: My neighbor swears the well water tastes different on Thursdays. I'm starting to believe it.
dialogue.chat.success/21: I found a button in my soup yesterday. Still don't know whose.
dialogue.chat.success/22: If you stack hay right, it's basically furniture. That's free wisdom.
dialogue.chat.success/23: The blacksmith hums when he thinks nobody's listening. It's always the same song.
dialogue.chat.success/24: One of the cats adopted me. I had no say in the matter.
dialogue.chat.success/25: I counted the fence posts on my street once. Forty-one. You needed to know that.
dialogue.story.success/10: One more? Alright — the year the river froze solid, we bowled with pumpkins on it.
dialogue.story.success/11: Did I tell you about the trader who sold maps to places he invented? Half the village still owns one.
dialogue.story.success/12: There was a rooster here once so mean it had its own warning sign. True story.
dialogue.story.success/13: My grandmother could predict rain with her knees. Never wrong. Terrifying woman.
dialogue.shake_hand.success/6: Firm grip! You'd survive market day.
dialogue.shake_hand.success/7: A proper handshake. Rarer than emeralds these days.
dialogue.shake_hand.success/8: Deal's a deal, whatever we just agreed to.
